newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU warns Milosevic over violence.
newsitem.headline: EU warns Milosevic over violence.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said on Tuesday he had warned Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic against a violent crackdown on peaceful opposition protests in Belgrade.
"I protested on behalf of the Union via the Dutch ambassador," he told a European Parliament committee. "They seem to be entering a new phase now. Violence will make everything different."
The Netherlands currently holds the presidency of the 15-nation.
But van Mierlo noted that the 15-nation bloc's influence on events in Serbia was limited. It already had a trade boycott, he said.
"The option for military intervention is more or less excluded. We are looking at political and diplomatic pressure.
"All we have left is to try to convince, to give moral support where it is needed and to see what we can do with the Americans."

Serbia's opposition has called for a campaign of passive resistance after the autocratic Milosevic ordered his riot police to forcibly break up pro-democracy demonstrations after 77 straight days of street protests.
On Monday, France invited leaders of the opposition party bloc to Paris, underlining growing Western support for democratisation in Serbia, under communist/socialist rule since 1945.

The European Union said in a statement issued in the Netherlands on Tuesday that it had been "dismayed by the police brutality against demonstrators in Belgrade this weekend, as well as reports of police brutality in other cities earlier last week."

"The use of violence against demonstrators cannot but aggravate the situation and lead to a total impasse in the current political crisis in the country. It will hamper any possible development of EU-FRY (Former Republic of Yugoslavia) relations in the near future," it added.
The 54-nation Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe also bemoaned the violence and called on Milosevic on Tuesday to begin talks with opposition groups.

It repeated its call for Milosevic to recognise opposition election wins in local elections last November and begin talks with the opposition on future democratic reforms, possibly under auspices of the OSCE.
